objections.claim: so inhibition runs against genetics; its rise is best read as a compensatory response.
objections.objection: The card tags approved anti-PD-L1 drugs but omits the clinical fact a gastroenterologist expects: checkpoint blockade itself causes enterocolitis and flares pre-existing IBD, which supports the genetic argument directly.
objections.suggestion: Add that PD-1/PD-L1 blockade causes immune-mediated enterocolitis and can flare UC, so the drug tag is a safety warning, not a repurposing lead.
objections.quote: Enterocolitis is among the leading adverse events associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs).

objections.claim: Placed above higher-ranked neutrophil genes because it is a change of the tissue itself
objections.objection: Presented as a new tissue target without the known negative result for the matrix metalloproteinase class in UC: the anti-MMP9 antibody andecaliximab failed its phase 2/3 induction trial.
objections.suggestion: Add that MMP inhibition has already failed in UC (andecaliximab, anti-MMP9), so MMP1 is a tissue-remodelling marker and any MMP1-selective approach needs that caveat.
objections.quote: Eight weeks of induction treatment with 150 mg andecaliximab in patients with UC did not induce clinical remission or response.

objections.claim: a tissue marker of neutrophil influx.
objections.objection: S100A8 is a subunit of calprotectin; any UC clinician will note the card omits that its protein is already the validated faecal calprotectin test, so it adds no new biomarker.
objections.suggestion: State that S100A8 with S100A9 forms calprotectin, the established faecal biomarker, and present the tissue rise as concordant with that test rather than as a candidate.
objections.quote: Quantification of the human S100A8/S100A9 tetrameric protein complex in stool, referred to as fecal calprotectin, is an extensively validated biomarker supporting the diagnosis and management of gastrointestinal diseases.
